subStrands.name: Selected Surahs

outcomes.text: read the selected surah for spiritual nourishment
recite the selected surah for use in devotional activities
explain the basic meaning of the selected surah to enhance positive character formation
apply the teachings of the selected surah in his/her daily life
appreciate the importance of the selected surahs by adhering to their teachings

learningExperiences: listen to the teacher/resource person or from a digital device recitation of the selected surahs
discuss the basic meaning of the selected surahs, in groups, and write in their notebook
listen to recorded translation of the selected surahs from a digital device
sort verses of the selected surahs with their corresponding meaning using digital devices/flash cards/ match individually/groups
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we recite suratul - Fatiha in every swalah?
Which surahs do Muslims recite before going to bed?
What lessons do we learn from the selected surahs?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening and teamwork are enhanced as learners discuss the basic meaning and lessons of the selected surah through group discussion.
Digital literacy: the skill of connecting using digital technology is enhanced through use of digital devices to listen to recorded translation of the selected surahs.
Creativity and imagination: the skill of making connection is enhanced as learners sort verses of the selected surahs with their corresponding meaning.
values: Responsibility: enhanced as learners sort verses of the selected surahs with their corresponding meaning using digital devices/flash cards/ match individually/groups
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learners work together in groups.
pcis: Citizenship: Social cohesion as learners discuss the lessons learnt from the selected surahs, in pairs or small groups.
links: As learners read selected surahs and relate reading skills in English and Kiswahili.

subStrands.name: Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as a Model of Good Character

outcomes.text: read the selected hadith on the character of the Prophet as a role model
analyse ways in which Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) is a model of good character
emulate the character of the Prophet in his/her daily life
value the Prophet as a role model by practising his character traits in daily life

learningExperiences: read the hadith: “I have been sent for the purpose of perfecting good morals.” (Narrated by Al-Hakim)
discuss ways in which Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) is a model of good character (trustworthy, truthful, kind, and generous) and present in class
role-play character traits of the Prophet
watch/listen to the story that portrays the character of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) from a digital device/teacher
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the character traits of a good child?
What were the character traits of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as a youth?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening and teamwork is enhanced as learners watch/listen to the story of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) from a digital device/teacher and discuss ways in which Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) is a model of good character.
Digital literacy: the skill of connecting using digital technology is enhanced through use of digital devices to listen to the story of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W).
values: Respect: is enhanced as learners listen attentively to the story of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) from a digital device/teacher.
Responsibility: as learners role-play character traits of the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).
pcis: Social cohesion: as learners role-play character traits of the Prophet
links: Creative Arts, as learner shows creativity as they role-play character traits of the Prophet.

subStrands.name: Hadith on Etiquette of Eating

outcomes.text: read the selected hadith on appropriate manners of eating
demonstrate the etiquette of eating to uphold the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.)
appreciate the etiquette of eating in accordance with the teachings of the Prophet (S.A.W.)

learningExperiences: read the hadith: “...Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right, and eat what is directly in front of you.” (Narrated by Al-Bukhari)
demonstrate the etiquette of eating individually/in small groups
role-play manners of eating
watch a video clip on good manners of eating
keyInquiryQuestions: What do you do before eating?
What is the benefit of saying Bismillah while eating?
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination: the skill of making connection is enhanced as learners role-play manners of eating.
Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners demonstrate the etiquette of eating with peers.
values: Respect, for other learners while demonstrating etiquette of eating together.
Responsibility, accountability as learners role-play manners of eating.
pcis: Self-esteem as learners collaborate with peers to demonstrate the etiquette of eating.
links: Agriculture as learners demonstrate the etiquette of eating individually/in small groups.

subStrands.name: Hadith on Brushing Teeth

outcomes.text: read the selected hadith on brushing teeth for the promotion of oral hygiene
assess the importance of brushing teeth as per the tradition of the Prophet (S.AW)
practise brushing teeth as an act of ibadah
appreciate the importance of brushing teeth to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.)

learningExperiences: read the hadith: “Brushing of teeth is a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.” (Narrated by Ibn Majah)
individually demonstrate how to brush his/her teeth
discuss the importance of brushing their teeth regularly
recite/sing song/qasida/poem on brushing teeth
keyInquiryQuestions: When do you brush your teeth?
Why do you brush your teeth?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced through discussing the importance of brushing their teeth regularly.
Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively through discussing the importance of brushing their teeth regularly in small groups.
Self-efficacy: as learners individually demonstrate how to brush their teeth and recite/sing song/qasida/poem on brushing teeth.
values: Responsibility: self-drive enhanced as learners individually demonstrate how to brush his/her teeth.
Respect: enhanced as learners respect each other’s view as they discuss the importance of brushing teeth.
pcis: Personal hygiene as learners brush their teeth.

subStrands.name: Hadith on Fitness

outcomes.text: read the selected hadith on physical fitness to promote healthy living
assess the importance of physical fitness in the life of a Muslim
participate in games and sports while observing Islamic values
value the importance of physical fitness as means of being dearer to Allah (S.W.T)

learningExperiences: read the hadith: “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.” (Narrated by Muslim)
discuss the importance of physical fitness and values derived from participating in games and sports (such as teamwork, sharing, humility, fair- play, discipline, and leadership skills)
discuss the types of games and sports permissible in Islam
discuss the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games and sports activities (dressing mode, observing times for swalah)
demonstrate the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should one be physically fit?
What Islamic rules should a Muslim observe while participating in games and sports activities?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced through discussing the importance of physical fitness and values derived from participating in games and sports.
Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners discuss the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games and sports activities.
Citizenship: the skill of social skills is enhanced as learners discuss the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games and sports activities.
values: Respect: acceptance is enhanced as learners respect each other opinion during discussion.
Responsibility: self-drive is enhanced as learners demonstrate etiquette to be observed during games.
pcis: Learner support programmes through participating in games and sports
links: Creative Arts: as they participate in various games and sports activities
Agriculture: by avoiding lifestyle diseases through exercises and promoting good health.

subStrands.name: Attributes of Allah (S.W.T)

outcomes.text: mention the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) with their corresponding meaning to strengthen the belief in Allah
apply the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) while making dua
appreciate the unique attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) as part of Islamic faith

learningExperiences: listen to the attributes of Allah from a digital device
sing qasida on the attributes of Allah
identify attributes of Allah and their corresponding meaning (Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, Al-Malik, AL-Salaam, AL- Samiu and Al- Basir)
match and sort the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) and their meaning
demonstrate reciting dua using the mentioned attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) individually or in pairs
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the favours of Allah (S.W.T.) to mankind?
What are the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.)?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced as learners discuss the unique attributes of Allah (S.W.T.), in pairs or small groups.
Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners listen to the attributes of Allah from a digital device.
Self-efficacy: the skill of self-awareness and planning is enhanced as learners sing qasida on the attributes of Allah.
Creativity and Imagination: the skill of making connection is enhanced as learners sort and match different attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) and their corresponding meaning.
values: Love is enhanced as learners sing qasida on the attributes of Allah.
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learners work collaboratively while discussing the unique attributes of Allah (S.W.T.).
Responsibility is enhanced as learners demonstrate how the duas are recited using the mentioned attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) individually or in pairs.
pcis: Self-esteem as learners recite duas that mention the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.).
links: English as learners acquire new vocabularies as they discuss the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) and their meaning.

subStrands.name: Belief in Angels

outcomes.text: mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith
explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman
appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

learningExperiences: name the angels of Allah, (Jibril, Mikail,Raqib and Atid, Izrail and Israfil)
match and sort the names of angels and their corresponding duties using flash cards/pocket boards
find names of angels from a crossword puzzle, in pairs or small groups
search and sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device
brainstorm on the duties of angels in their lives, in pairs or small groups, and write the points in their notebook
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the duties of angels?
Why did Allah (S.W.T.) create angels?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skills of speaking and writing are enhanced as learners discuss the significance of angels in their lives, in pairs or small groups, and write their points in their notebooks.
Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of interpretation and inference is enhanced as learners find names of angels from a crossword puzzle, in pairs or small groups.
Self–efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device.
values: Responsibility: self-drive as learners search and sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device.
Respect: open-mindedness as learners respect each other’s opinions as they discuss the significance of angels in their lives.
pcis: Self-awareness as learners will be cautious in carrying out his duties.
links: English: reading skills as learners acquire new vocabularies while discussing the names of angels and their duties.

subStrands.name: Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an
content: Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience)

outcomes.text: mention the twenty-five prophets of Allah (S.W.T.) in the Qur’an
analyse the virtues of the prophets of Allah for character formation
apply the virtues of the prophets of Allah in their daily life
acknowledge the belief in the prophets of Allah as a Pillar of Iman

learningExperiences: identify fellow learners named after prophets
name the prophets of Allah in the Qur’an (Q.4:163-165, 6:84-86, 21: 85-88) and write in their notebook
describe the virtues (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) of the prophets in pairs or small groups, and write the points in their notebook
dramatise/role-play how they can apply the virtues of the prophets in their daily life
keyInquiryQuestions: What virtues do we learn from these prophets?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skills of speaking and writing are enhanced as learners name the prophets of Allah and write them in their notebook.
Creativity and imagination: the skill is enhanced as learners dramatise/role-play how they can apply the virtues of the prophets of Allah in their daily life.
Citizenship: social and civic skills are enhanced as learners discuss the virtues (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) of the prophets, in pairs or small groups.
values: Social justice equity enhanced as learners dramatise/role-play how they can apply the virtues of the prophets in their daily life.
pcis: Self-esteem as learners name prophets mentioned in the Qur’an.
links: Social Studies: as learners discuss the virtues exhibited by the prophets of Allah S.W.T., which is related to good governance.

subStrands.name: Twahara (Ritual Purity)

outcomes.text: outline the types of najasaat (impurities) for physical and spiritual purification
demonstrate appropriate ways of cleaning najasaat (impurities) for the purpose of purification
acknowledge ritual cleanliness as a condition for ibadah

learningExperiences: name the different types of najasaat (mukhaffafah or light, mutawassitah or medium, and mughalladha or heavy)
discuss items used in the purification of najasa and present in class
demonstrate how to purify different najasaat individually/in pairs/in groups
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you purify najasaat?
What items do you use in removing najasaat?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration the skill of team work is enhanced as learners discuss items used in the purification of najasa, in pairs or small groups, and present in class
Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of explanation is enhanced as learners discuss items used in the purification of najasa, in pairs or small groups, and present in class
Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge as learners demonstrate how to purify different najasaat, individually/in pairs/in groups
values: Responsibility: enhanced as learners demonstrate how to purify different najasaat, individually/in pairs/in groups
pcis: Health Issues: Personal hygiene through maintenance of ritual cleanliness.
links: Agriculture as learners observe and maintain cleanliness.

subStrands.name: Wudhu (Ablution)

outcomes.text: state the nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) to maintain a state of ritual purity
assess the significance of wudhu in the life of a Muslim
value the need to be in a state of purity as a condition for ibadah

learningExperiences: search for nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook
discuss times recommended to be in a state of wudhu and present in class
discuss the importance of maintaining wudhu and be guided to write the points in their notebook
keyInquiryQuestions: What nullifies wudhu?
Why is it important to be in a state of wudhu?
When is it recommended to be in a state of wudhu?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing is enhanced as learners search for nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook.
Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners discuss times recommended to be in a state of wudhu and present in class.
values: Unity: cooperation enhanced as learners discuss the importance of maintaining wudhu, in pairs or groups.
Responsibility: hard work enhanced as learners search for nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook.
pcis: Personal hygiene as learners perform wudhu.
links: Agriculture as learners observe and maintain ritual purity.

subStrands.name: Conditions for Swalah

outcomes.text: state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity
demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life
acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity

learningExperiences: mention the conditions for swalah and write them in their notebook
discuss the conditions for swalah and present in class
demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually
demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices/direction of the sun in identifying direction of Qibla, individually/in pairs/groups
discuss how to determine times for swalah and present in class
keyInquiryQuestions: How would you identify time for swalah and direction of Qibla
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices in identifying direction of Qibla.

Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of interpretation and inference is enhanced as learners demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices/direction of the sun in identifying direction of Qibla, individually/in pairs/groups
Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually.
values: Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learners work together to discuss the conditions for swalah, in pairs or groups, and present in class
Respect: enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion as they discuss how to determine times for swalah, in pairs /groups, and present in class
pcis: Health issues: Personal hygiene as a requirement for swalah
links: Social Studies: as learners learn finding directions on the compass.

subStrands.name: Pillars of Swalah

outcomes.text: identify the pillars of prayers for validity of swalah
apply the pillars of swalah correctly in daily prayers
appreciate the need for observing the pillars of swalah by emulating the Sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.)

learningExperiences: pick the pillars of swalah (niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram, reciting al-Fatiha, rukuu, raising from rukuu, sujud, siting between the sujud, sitting while reciting the last tashahhud, tashahhud, prayers for Ibrahim, taslim, tumaninah, tartib) from a flash cards and arrange them in sequence
discuss the pillars of swalah and write them in their notebook
role-play the pillars of swalah, individually/in pairs/in groups
watch a video clip of pillars of swalah on digital device
demonstrate the pillars of swalah, individually/in pairs/in groups
keyInquiryQuestions: What do you recite when praying?
Which postures are performed in prayers?
coreCompetencies: Learning to Learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners discuss the pillars of swalah, in pairs/groups, and be guided to write them in their notebook.
Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing and speaking is enhanced as learners discuss the pillars of swalah, in pairs/groups, and be guided to write them in their notebook
Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners role-play the pillars of swalah, individually/in pairs/in groups
values: Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners role-play the pillars of swalah, individually/in pairs/in groups.
Unity: cooperation enhanced as learners demonstrate the pillars of swalah, in pairs/groups.
pcis: Health issues: Postures of swalah prevent lifestyles diseases, which promotes good health.
links: Creative Arts as learners perform the pillars of swalah, which is part of exercise.
